Publication-Ready ggplot2 Theme for Single-Cell QC Figures

Source: R/theme_prepro.R
theme_prepro.Rd

A clean, minimal ggplot2 theme tuned for the QC figures this package produces – per-sample violins, count distributions, faceted density grids. Axis titles are always bold, secondary text (subtitle, caption, legend) is set in muted grey, and panel furniture is kept recessive so the data carries the figure.

Usage

theme_prepro(
  style = c("clean", "airy", "frame"),
  base_size = 13,
  base_family = ""
)

Arguments

style

Panel style: one of "clean" (default), "airy" or "frame". See Details.

base_size

Base font size in points. All other text is sized relative to this, so this is the one knob to turn when a figure is destined for a small multi-panel layout. Default 13.

base_family

Base font family. Defaults to "" (the device's default sans-serif), which keeps figures portable across machines. Set to e.g. "Helvetica" or "Arial" to match a journal's requirements.

Value

A complete ggplot2 theme object, to be added to a plot with +.

Details

Three panel styles are available. They share identical typography and differ only in how the panel is framed, so figures built from a mix of styles still read as one set:

"clean"

No gridlines; a hairline L-shaped axis with ticks. The classic journal figure. Best for violins and boxplots, where shape matters more than reading exact values off the axis.

"airy"

Faint horizontal rules only, with no axis lines or ticks – the grid stands in for the axis. Best when a reader needs to compare heights across samples, such as median UMI count or percent mitochondrial reads.

"frame"

A boxed panel with a dotted grid and tinted facet strips, and the legend moved to the top so wide facet grids keep their horizontal room. Best for multi-panel figures where each facet needs a visible boundary.

The theme is complete in the ggplot2 sense, so it replaces the active theme rather than adding to it. Override any individual element by adding a further ggplot2::theme() call after it.

See also

scale_fill_prepro() and scale_colour_prepro() for the matching colour scales, prepro_pal() for the palette itself.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)

seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(path = "/path/to/Pool1/outs", multi = TRUE)
seurat      <- mergeSeurat(seurat_list)

# UMI counts per cell, one violin per sample
ggplot(seurat@meta.data, aes(x = Ident, y = nCount_RNA, fill = Ident)) +
    geom_violin(scale = "width", colour = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.11, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white") +
    scale_y_log10() +
    scale_fill_prepro() +
    labs(title = "UMI counts per cell", x = NULL, y = "nCount_RNA") +
    theme_prepro("clean") +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

# the same data as a faceted density grid
ggplot(seurat@meta.data, aes(x = nCount_RNA, fill = Ident)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.55) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_fill_prepro() +
    facet_wrap(~ Ident) +
    theme_prepro("frame")
} # }
